close_reason: 13 chat-server sites migrated to .expect(...) in commit 65646cf; workspace-wide propagation of the same pattern (~106 sites across siblings) filed as bd:JMAP-oehi.
description:
16 sites across two test files use `.unwrap_or("")` or `.unwrap_or(usize::MAX)` to extract values from `serde_json::Value` before asserting on them:

- role_member_apply.rs:170, 296, 576, 768, 923 — `.as_str().unwrap_or("")` followed by `assert!(desc.contains("manage_roles"))` (5 sites)
- channel_category_apply.rs:198, 235, 265, 330, 510, 520, 576, 584 — same pattern, plus the `.unwrap_or(usize::MAX)` variants for array-length checks (9 sites)

Example (channel_category_apply.rs:517-524):

    let chan_count = get_resp["list"][0]["uncategorizedChannelIds"]
        .as_array()
        .map(Vec::len)
        .unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
    assert_eq!(chan_count, 0, "...");

`unwrap_or(usize::MAX)` here is defensive theatre — if the field isn't an array, the test should fail loudly with 'expected array, got null' rather than coincidentally satisfying `!= 0` with a nonsense sentinel. Worse, in a future refactor where the assertion becomes `<= N` for some moderate N, the `usize::MAX` sentinel would PASS a buggy code path that was supposed to be a regression test.

Similarly, `.unwrap_or("")` then `assert!(desc.contains("manage_roles"))` will silently emit a confusing 'contains failed: ""' diagnostic if the field is absent, rather than 'expected description field to be a string but it was null'.

Idiomatic Rust: `.expect("uncategorizedChannelIds must be an array")` and `.expect("description must be a string")`. Tests want loud, named failures, not silent fallthrough into confusing later assertions.

Engineering basis: concrete bug-hiding path. A future schema change that drops the `description` field entirely would not flag any of these tests — they would `unwrap_or("")` and then `false.contains(...)` to a confusing assert failure rather than the obvious 'the field isn't there' failure. The `usize::MAX` case is the worst — it's a sentinel value actively chosen to make negative-direction assertions pass artificially, which is the opposite of what a test should do.
title: tests: .unwrap_or("") and .unwrap_or(usize::MAX) in assertion paths hide schema-shape failures with confusing diagnostics
